issues.description: The solution repository implements SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal classes instead of the Goat, Pig, and Seal classes named in the problem statement and UML. Additionally, Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java in the solution are empty. This name/type mismatch between the expected class names (Goat, Pig, Seal) and the actual solution classes (SpaceGoat, SpacePig, SpaceSeal) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and may cause tests or examples that reference Goat/Pig/Seal to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Either provide concrete implementations named Goat, Pig, and Seal in the solution repository (implementing the specified interfaces and behavior), or update the problem statement and UML to consistently use the SpaceGoat/SpacePig/SpaceSeal names. Ensure the solution contains non-empty Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java classes with the expected constructors and method implementations so students and tests referencing those exact class names are not confused or broken.

issues.description: The problem statement and template reference animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution repository provides implementations named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This mismatch (presence of Space* classes instead of the expected Seal/Pig/Goat) creates a naming-mapping barrier: students reading the task and the template will look for Seal/Pig/Goat implementations, while the solution uses different identifiers, increasing extraneous cognitive load and risking confusion about the intended class names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make class names consistent across artifacts. Either rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat, or update the problem statement and template to reference SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. Alternatively, provide thin wrapper classes named Seal/Pig/Goat that delegate to the corresponding Space* implementations so the expected identifiers in the exercise remain available.
